records.issue_text: [BUG] The matcher reads the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5), but the encoded layout is sessionType(2 chars)+tokenType(2 chars)+grantType(2 chars), so the grant shortcut occupies substring(4, 6). The matcher compares a window straddling the last char of tokenType and the first char of grantType (e.g. for 'acrtac' it compares 'rt'), so even with the inverted logic fixed it never inspects the actual grant type and the assertion is meaningless for its stated purpose.
records.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the code extracts the grant shortcut with `items[0].substring(3, 5)` (see added matcher). But the token id is encoded as `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2) + ':' + rawId` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`, meaning the grant shortcut is at indices 4–5 (`substring(4, 6)`). Using `substring(3,5)` straddles the last char of tokenType and first char of grantType, so it never correctly validates the grant type as intended. Additionally, the matcher’s equality check is inverted: `if ( ... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`

records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId's matching logic is inverted and reads the wrong character positions: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns 'no match' exactly when the grant shortcut matches. The encoded context is 6 chars (e.g. "onrtac"): grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5, but substring(3,5) reads indices 3-4 ("ta"), so the grant is never actually verified; and because equality is negated, a token whose chars 3-4 happen to equal the expected grant shortcut is declared a non-match while any other value falls through to the UUID check and passes. The matcher is a stand-in guard that passes for arbitrary grant types and fails for the one arrangement it names, so every expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertion green-lights tokens with wrong grant encoding.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] grantType is snapshotted once in the constructor from formParams, but the class still exposes setFormParams() which can replace the form params afterwards without updating grantType. Callers that build a Context and then swap in different form params (the pattern the deleted copy-constructor was used for, e.g. device grant building a derived context) get a stale grantType baked into the access token's jti prefix, so the encoded context misreports the grant that actually produced the token — exactly the drift the encoder exists to prevent.

Any already-compiled custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (a supported extension point, since this lives in server-spi-private but grants are pluggable via META-INF/services) throws AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut(); because postInit runs at server bootstrap, the entire Keycloak instance fails to start, not just the custom grant — an upgrade with no migration path for custom grants.
